title: Assembly manifest: the single truth of how the system runs, as pure data
description: The language-neutral canon of the assembly manifest. Developers generate it with a typed API; ordinary users have a UI or an agent write it for them; the kernel only faithfully executes it. Every wire in black and white — version-controlled, diffable. This schema pins local structure only; cross-referential rules (instances reference registered components, ports exist and face the right way, wire type compatibility) belong to assembly inspection.

instances.description: Instance name → which component, with what config; "core" is reserved for kernel-recorded events

wires.description: Every wire, in black and white

component.description: Component name, looked up in the component registry

config.description: Component-private config, any JSON value; the kernel does not interpret it

requires.description: The slot's bound (the trait bound of assemblies): profiles whatever fills this position must claim. Inspection rejects the assembly when the component does not implement every listed profile — an unqualified swap fails at boot with a plain message. Omitted or empty = no requirement.

endpoint.description: "instance.port" — everything before the first dot is the instance
